en: What is the longest fence in the world, and what is it trying to keep out?
I'm Max, and this is Max Wise.
It runs for about five thousand six hundred kilometers, across three Australian states.
That's roughly the distance from London to New York.
Most of it is wire mesh, about six feet tall.
Its job is to keep out this guy, the dingo.
It's a wild dog, about the size of a medium pet dog.
Dingoes can sprint at around sixty kilometers per hour, and they hunt kangaroos and smaller animals.
Then, in the late seventeen hundreds, Europeans arrived and brought sheep.
To a hungry dingo, that was a brand new menu.
Farmers tried traps and guns, but they kept losing sheep.
So in the eighteen eighties, they started building fences.
Over the years, those fences were joined into one giant barrier.
Sheep country on one side, most dingoes on the other.
